chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to him regarding a man who did not find water, and the salat (prayer) became due, so he performed tayammum and prayed two rak'ahs; then he found water: should he invalidate the two rak'ahs, or cut them off and perform wudu (ablution), then pray? He said: No, rather he should continue in his salat (prayer) and not invalidate them, because he entered it while he was in a state of taharah and had performed tayammum.

Zurarah said: So I said to him: He entered it while being in tayammum, then prayed one rak'ah and broke his wudu, then found water. He said: He should leave, perform wudu (ablution), and build upon what has passed of his salat (prayer) which he prayed with tayammum.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: entered a state of ritual impurity by nullifying purification
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer already performed
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute for wudu (ablution) due to lack of water
key_terms.مُتَيَمِّمٌ: one who is in a state of purity through tayammum
key_terms.يَبْنِي: continues the prayer based on what has already been completed

ai.seo_question: If someone starts salat (prayer) with tayammum and then finds water, should the prayer be stopped or continued?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings related to tayammum during salat (prayer) when water is later found. If one began the prayer in a valid state of ritual purity through tayammum, finding water does not require invalidating the prayer; however, if one becomes ritually impure during the prayer and then finds water, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues from what has already been prayed.
